newsitem.title: UK: UK's OFT to crack down on high risk loan companies.
newsitem.headline: UK's OFT to crack down on high risk loan companies.

text.p: The UK's Office of Fair Trading on Friday announced guidelines to loan companies which offer mortgages and other secured loans to people with poor credit ratings.

John Bridgeman, the Director General of Fair Trading, said lenders and brokers in the "non-status" market had been told to "end oppressive dual interest rate schemes and inappropriate penalties for early settlements in guidelines issued today".
Lenders and brokers who ignore the guidelines risk losing their credit licences.

"The guidelines highlight some of the main practices which I consider to be deceitful or oppressive, or otherwise unfair or improper -- whether unlawful or not -- and which, if continued, will lead me to take regulatory action against those involved," Bridgeman said in a statement.
The guidelines follow continued complaints about the business practices of some lenders and brokers in the non-status lending market, despite an earlier warning in February.
Complaints included those of consumers being persuaded to take out loans beyond their ability to repay and insufficient information or time to consider the agreements before signing.
Two issues that gave rise to complaints relate to early redemption and "concessionary" interest rates.
A mortgage or loan is often sold on a concessionary rate but a much higher "standard" rate becomes payable if there is a payment default.

"Such dual interest rates have misled consumers," said Bridgeman. "Further, dual interest rates, particularly those with a large differential between the two rates, are unfair and oppressive and may well be unenforceable.
Lenders should also stop "at the earliest opportunity" use of 'Rule of 78' for the early settlement of loans which amounts to a penalty on early settlement.
Bridgeman said he intended to write to lenders and brokers during September to see what action they had taken.

Among companies whose share prices were hit in May by reports the government was reviewing firms specialising in lending to the poor are: Provident Financial Plc, Cattles Plc and London Scottish Bank Plc.
